clue.text: Altered by lie, altered by design

indicators.note: the second 'altered' says the three preceding words have been changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Something changed by a falsehood, then changed again on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'Altered' looks like the indicator, but it is fodder; the second 'altered' rearranges ALTERED BY LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by design means doing it on purpose, intentionally rather than by accident.

clue.text: Crab maybe walked about, almost curious

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the synonym for walked is read backwards

parts.note: to have paced is to have walked

indicators.note: almost means the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: curious means odd, strange

explanation.surface: A crab walking sideways around something, looking rather odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns PACED into DECAP; 'almost' cuts ODD to OD.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs belong to the ten-legged crustacean order, so a crab is an example; 'maybe' flags it.

clue.text: Light unit measurement's European norm initially

definitions.text: Light unit measurement's European norm initially

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A description of a standard unit for measuring light, as fixed across Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The heads of the five words spell the answer, and the whole clue also describes it: an SI unit, the standard used in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the SI unit of luminous flux, the standard measure of emitted light.

clue.text: Blast resounded round exhaust's opening in backfire

indicators.note: round means the two synonyms sit either side of the letter that follows

parts.note: a blast is a boom, a loud explosion
a bell that resounded rang

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A car exhaust backfiring with a loud bang that echoes around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backfire' is the verb sense: a scheme that rebounds on its maker, like the curved throwing stick returning.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan that will boomerang rebounds on its maker, the figurative sense of backfiring.

clue.text: Grasses Sun up!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: the Sun is a star

explanation.surface: An exclamation about lawns or meadows at sunrise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns STAR backwards. 'Grasses' is a verb: to grass is British slang for informing to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To grass on someone and to rat on them are both slang for informing, betraying to authorities.

clue.text: Afflictions of soldiers, male, under canvas?

indicators.note: under canvas means sheltering inside tents, so the soldiers and male go inside

parts.note: canvas stands for tents, as in camping under canvas
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Asking what troubles a camping soldier suffers.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is short for 'other ranks', the enlisted soldiers of the British army; 'under canvas' means camping in tents.
explanation.definitionFit: Torments are sufferings or agonies, so they are afflictions, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Boy, even empty, carrying some weight

parts.note: a boy is a lad

indicators.note: empty means the word is emptied of its middle, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A boy, even with nothing in his hands, still bearing a load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves EN from even.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means loaded or burdened, so something laden is bearing a load.

clue.text: Tendency to include reading perhaps for education

indicators.note: to include means the letter for reading is put inside the tendency word

parts.note: a leaning is a tendency or inclination
R stands for reading, one of the three Rs of schooling

explanation.surface: A tendency to read as a route to becoming educated.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'three Rs' are reading, writing and arithmetic, so R can stand for any of them; 'perhaps' flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning is knowledge gained by study, so it is a synonym for education.

clue.text: Pungent air around middle of restroom

indicators.note: around means the tune word goes round the central letters

parts.note: an air is a tune, a song

indicators.note: the middle of an eight-letter word is its central two letters

explanation.surface: A sharp smell hanging in a public lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' is a tune here, not the atmosphere the smell suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong smell is a powerful, pungent one, so the two are synonyms here.

clue.text: Part in sitcom for terrible dummy

indicators.note: part in means the letters lie within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A dreadful dummy taking a role in a TV comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: A dummy here is the British word for a baby's pacifier, also called a comforter.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English both words name the rubber teat a baby sucks to be soothed.

clue.text: Stayed saucy, twirling with tango

indicators.note: twirling means turning round, so the word for saucy is reversed

parts.note: saucy can mean lewd, smutty
Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone stayed on the dance floor, being cheeky while spinning in a tango.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twirling' turns LEWD into DWEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To have dwelt somewhere is to have lived or remained there, so it means stayed.

clue.text: More feeble play on words? That is right

parts.note: a pun is a play on words
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A judgement that a pun is weaker, then a conclusion that this is right.
explanation.definitionFit: Puny means weak or small, so its comparative form means weaker or more feeble.

clue.text: Age taken by fat old painter?

indicators.note: taken by means the age word is absorbed into the fat word

parts.note: lard is pig fat
an eon (aeon) is an age

explanation.surface: An old painter who grew stout with age.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: the Renaissance master da Vinci.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci was a Renaissance artist, so he is one example of a painter.

clue.text: Husband is maybe hiding alarm

indicators.note: hiding means the answer is concealed within the words that come before it

explanation.surface: A husband possibly concealing his worry.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay is a feeling of consternation or alarm, so the two are synonyms as nouns.

clue.text: Right in America upset, albeit wrongly

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: US is short for United States, America

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters of albeit are arranged in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone in the US gets angry, though wrongly, about what is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns US into SU; 'wrongly' rearranges ALBEIT into ITABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suitable is fitting or appropriate, which is one sense of right.

clue.text: Storing remains covered by incense

indicators.note: covered by means the word for remains is held inside the word for incense

parts.note: to incense is to anger or provoke, to sting
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Something burnt left beneath a layer of fragrant incense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incense' is a verb, to anger, not the fragrant smoke the ash suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Stashing means hiding away for later use, so it means storing.

clue.text: Wrong keeping head of cattle, cultivate a grain

indicators.note: keeping means the word for wrong holds the letter that follows

parts.note: a wrong is a sin

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to till the soil is to cultivate it

explanation.surface: A farming scene: it is wrong to keep cattle on land that should grow grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' gives C from cattle, kept inside SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace or particle, just as a grain can mean the smallest amount.

clue.text: Annihilate multitude about to catch a cold

indicators.note: to catch means the following letters are caught inside the earlier pieces

parts.note: a mass is a multitude, a great number
re means about, concerning
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A huge crowd is on the verge of catching a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like the container signal, but it gives its own letters; 'to catch' does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: To massacre is to slaughter in great numbers, so it can mean to wipe out or annihilate.

clue.text: Drift catching current finally hooking fish

indicators.note: catching means the word for drift holds the pieces that follow

parts.note: to drift is to stray, wander off course
in means current, fashionable

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An angler drifting on a current catching a fish on a hook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like a flow of water or electricity, but here it means fashionable, as in 'in vogue'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat cartilaginous sea creature with a barbed tail, a kind of fish.

clue.text: Break from Church doctrine's first in diocese

indicators.note: in means the church letters plus the initial go inside the diocese word

parts.note: a bishop's see is his diocese
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of doctrine

explanation.surface: A doctrinal dispute leads to a split from the Church within a diocese.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is the area a bishop governs; CE stands for the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To secede is to withdraw formally from a body or union, so it means to break away from it.

clue.text: Gorged showing greed oddly, after wine case

indicators.note: after means the odd letters come behind the wine case word

parts.note: a bin is a rack or case for storing wine

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Someone stuffed themselves greedily after getting into a case of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' gives GED from greed.
explanation.definitionFit: To have binged is to have eaten or drunk to excess, so it means gorged.

clue.text: Stood for action holding weight lifted

indicators.note: holding means the action word contains the reversed weight

parts.note: a deed is an action

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means raised up, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A weightlifter standing in for someone in the action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' suggests the weightlifting picture, but in a down entry it signals the weight is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A symbol that denoted something signified or represented it, the sense of stood for.

clue.text: Punish hound taking common order rolling over

indicators.note: taking means the hound word takes the reversed order inside it

parts.note: to hound someone is to chase them

indicators.note: rolling over means the order word is turned backwards

parts.note: sit is a common order given to a dog

explanation.surface: Disciplining a dog that rolls over instead of obeying a command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hound' is a verb, to pursue, not the dog the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise is to scold or discipline severely, so it is a synonym of punish.

clue.text: An American writer or two?

explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain was a US novelist; the same word is also an old term meaning a pair.

clue.text: America can, employing army, win

indicators.note: employing means the can word takes the army inside it

parts.note: a tin is a can
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A rallying cry: America can win by using its army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is a noun, a tin, not the verb the rallying cry suggests; TA is Britain's Territorial Army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain a goal is to achieve or gain it, the sense of win as in win a prize.

clue.text: Tall story with article about extraterrestrial

indicators.note: about means the article goes around the tall story

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a tall story is a lie

explanation.surface: A far-fetched tale in a newspaper article about a visitor from space.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a being from another world, which is what an extraterrestrial is.

clue.text: Sentence is overturned leading to discharge

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: time is a prison sentence, as in doing time

explanation.surface: A court sentence overturned on appeal, leading to a prisoner's release.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to give off or send out, so it means discharge as a verb.

clue.text: Greek character central to 'Medea'?

parts.note: the central letter of Medea is D, and the Greek letter for D is the one named

explanation.surface: Asking which figure is at the heart of Euripides' Greek tragedy Medea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a figure in the play, but it is a letter of the Greek alphabet: the middle letter of MEDEA.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet, equivalent to D, which sits in the middle of Medea.

clue.text: Politician rested in bed for illness …

indicators.note: in means the politician and rested words go inside the bed word

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
MP is a Member of Parliament
to have lain is to have rested

explanation.surface: A politician has been laid up in bed with some sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: MP means Member of Parliament, a British politician; a cot is a small bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can mean an ailment or disorder, so it is a synonym of illness.

clue.text: … strangely ensured it ran wild

indicators.note: strangely means the letters of the next three words are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: Continuing the sick politician: their illness made sure it spread out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrestrained means without checks or limits, which is what wild behaviour is.
